takeaways: The 10-year Treasury blew through 5.12% on Sept. 23 — its highest since 2007 — as hot PMI data fueled bets on another Fed hike. With $875B of commercial mortgages maturing in 2026, refi math just got harder for every leveraged owner.

Institutional capital is converging on senior housing: MetLife, Apollo and Cushman panelists at CO's forum called it the next asset class to institutionalize, and Welltower's record Q2 (SHOP occupancy 89.4%, RevPOR +5.2%) backs the thesis.

A $380M, 221-unit CCRC broke ground in Boynton Beach — the first new life plan community there since 2016 and 70%+ presold — a live signal that South Florida demand is deep enough to underwrite ground-up again.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury tops 5.12%, highest since 2007, on hot PMI data
items.summary: The 10-year yield surged above 5.12% on Sept. 23 after S&P Global's PMI showed private-sector activity expanding at its fastest pace in five years with accelerating price pressures, reviving expectations of a second Fed hike this year. Higher long rates flow straight into commercial mortgage coupons, construction loans and CMBS pricing. For Lloyd Jones, in-place cash flow and early refinancing execution now matter more than pro forma growth.

items.headline: $875B CRE maturity wall collides with Fed's first hike since 2023
items.summary: MBA data shows $875B (17%) of the $5T in outstanding commercial mortgages matures in 2026, just as the Fed lifted rates to 3.75%–4.00% with PPI at 5.4% and oil above $100. Trepp's special servicing rate hit 11.42%, the highest since 2013, and Realmo shows office, industrial and hotel sale listings down 20–38% since July while multifamily listings rose 21%. A $5M interest-only loan rolling from 4% to 7.25% adds $162,500 a year in debt service — expect more motivated sellers and thinner concession budgets.

items.headline: Institutional investors: senior housing is the next asset class to institutionalize
items.summary: At Commercial Observer's Institutional & Private Equity Forum, MetLife IM's William Pattison predicted senior housing and medical office will be as institutionalized as apartments and industrial within a decade, and Apollo's Bert Crouch called senior living a 'secular thematic conviction.' Blackstone's Katie Keenan flagged multi-decade-low supply in multifamily and Middle Eastern capital returning to the U.S. as a safe haven. Strong validation of the Lloyd Jones thesis and a signal that LP appetite for the sector is growing.

items.headline: $380M Boynton Beach CCRC breaks ground, 70% presold, first since 2016
items.summary: Nonprofit Green Cay Life Plan Village started construction on The Winsberg at Green Cay, a $380M, 221-unit continuing care community (189 IL, 32 AL/MC) in Boynton Beach, with Greenbrier Development and BRP Senior Housing Management co-developing and Moss as CM; opening is slated for fall 2028. It is the first new CCRC in Boynton Beach since 2016, sits on the last fully entitled site of its kind in Palm Beach County, and has 70%+ of IL units under contract. A direct competitive and demand signal in Lloyd Jones's South Florida backyard.

items.headline: Canadian senior living deals hit record $8B as occupancy nears 95%
items.summary: Senior housing and care transaction volume in Canada reached $8B year-to-date, shattering the 2007 record of $4.9B, while average occupancy climbed to 94%, up 2.5 points year over year, with operators on track for 95% by year-end. The Canadian market is a preview of what constrained supply plus boomer demand does to pricing and deal velocity. Cross-border capital chasing yield there could tighten competition for U.S. stabilized assets too.

items.headline: Economists call 7% mortgages the 'new normal' after Fed hike
items.summary: NAR's Lawrence Yun said 7% mortgage rates may be a 'new normal,' MBA's Mike Fratantoni forecasts two more hikes over the next year, and NAHB's Robert Dietz warned higher AD&C loan costs will further choke new construction. For senior housing owners, higher-for-longer means costlier refis and construction debt, but it also keeps new supply suppressed, supporting occupancy and rate growth in existing communities.

items.headline: The Springs Living partners with SCAN to bring Medicare Advantage I-SNP to residents
items.summary: Oregon operator The Springs Living is partnering with SCAN Health Plan, one of the largest nonprofit Medicare Advantage plans, to offer its Institutional Special Needs Plan across more than 1,900 residences in the Portland area. The deal follows Curana Health's I-SNP launch for Iowa senior living residents last week. Operator-aligned I-SNPs are becoming a standard lever for reducing hospitalizations, lengthening stays and capturing a share of medical spend — worth evaluating for Lloyd Jones's assisted living portfolio.

items.headline: Welltower posts record Q2: SHOP occupancy 89.4%, RevPOR up 5.2%
items.summary: Welltower, the largest senior housing owner with 130,957 units across 1,184 properties, reported record normalized FFO of $1.60 per share versus $0.65 consensus, with same-store SHOP occupancy at 89.4% and RevPOR growth of 5.2%; its market cap now sits near $173.7B. Meanwhile Discovery overtook Brookdale as the largest operator in the 2026 ASHA 50 as Brookdale's footprint shrank to 42,697 units. Only ~1,000 construction starts per quarter face 2 million Americans turning 80 this year.

items.headline: Nonprofit life plan communities post strongest profitability gains in a decade
items.summary: Fitch Ratings reports not-for-profit life plan communities closed 2025 with their largest year-over-year profitability improvement in ten years, driven by rising occupancy, moderating expense growth and lower agency staffing as retention stabilized. Leverage remains the sector's main headwind. The margin recovery at nonprofits, which compete directly with for-profit IL/AL, suggests pricing power is holding across the board.

items.headline: NACD: boards, not Congress, will decide how fast AI gets deployed
items.summary: Fortune's Ryan McManus (NACD New York) argues most companies are stuck in an AI 'crawl': AI is the top board agenda item for 65% of public-company directors, yet only 22% of S&P 500 companies disclose board AI oversight and just 29% of leaders say their boards have the right expertise. He cites Ford's failed attempt to replace veteran engineers with 900 AI inspection cameras before recovering by pairing AI with rehired experts. Lesson for operators: start with strategy and human-augmenting pilots, not headcount cuts.

items.headline: Claude now leads 26% of Anthropic's R&D; Nvidia sees chip sales doubling in 2027
items.summary: Anthropic's R&D Automation Index shows Claude led 26% of its model research by August, up from under 1% in February, with roughly 30,000 agents at work; Nvidia's Jensen Huang said the company expects to sell twice as many chips next year after $96.2B in quarterly revenue (+106% YoY). Security flags the same week: a Brevo supply-chain attack hit 100,000+ websites. Agentic AI is compounding fast — and vendor security diligence should scale with it.

items.headline: Proptech's next frontier: an AI 'decision layer' spanning senior living to rentals
items.summary: Inman profiles the Infinityy and Local Logic partnership, which pairs AI-guided property exploration with neighborhood intelligence across multifamily, student housing, senior living, hospitality and office. The thesis: a senior living prospect and a renter face the same 'is this place right for me' decision, yet for-rent marketing remains transactional rather than educational. Relevant to senior housing sales teams fighting prospect analysis paralysis and long decision cycles.

items.headline: JM Search: 59% of CEOs who feel underpaid weighed leaving in past six months
items.summary: JM Search's 2026 CEO Compensation & Insights Study of 350 CEOs and presidents, heavily PE-backed, found 85% rank equity and long-term upside among their top two pay elements, the clearest comp step-up happens at $250M in revenue, and 59% of CEOs who feel paid below market considered leaving in the prior six months versus 37% of those at or above market. 76% cite growth and operational execution as their top pressure, with talent second. A useful benchmark for executive retention at the operating-company level.

items.headline: Longevity biotech market pegged at $617B as pharma appetite grows
items.summary: A Longevity.Technology report relayed by the Global Wellness Summit maps more than 3,000 therapeutic assets and sizes the longevity biotech market at $617B, noting that capital, pipelines and pharma interest are now moving in step. Healthspan — cognitive sharpness, mobility, prevention — is displacing 'anti-aging' as the organizing idea. A tailwind narrative for wellness-forward senior living positioning and longer, healthier independent-living tenancies.

items.headline: PLACE acquires Maxwell, mortgage tech touching $130B in annual volume
items.summary: Proptech PLACE bought Denver-based Maxwell, whose point-of-sale, fulfillment and AI business-intelligence tools serve 400+ banks, credit unions and lenders and touch about $130B in annual mortgage volume; CEO John Paasonen and 100+ staff stay on. It follows PLACE's earlier 2026 purchase of Radian's Real Estate Services unit. Residential-focused, but another marker of proptech consolidation as job postings in the sector fell 59% in three months.

items.headline: Data centers took a record 14.4% of new industrial leasing; 279 moratoriums now active
items.summary: Cushman & Wakefield data cited by CRE Direct shows data-center tenants captured a record 14.4% of new industrial leasing last year and are bidding directly against logistics developers for sites. Local pushback is escalating: active data-center moratoriums nationwide surged to 279 through September from just 16 a year earlier. Land pricing and power access in Sun Belt submarkets are increasingly shaped by hyperscaler demand.

items.headline: JLL creates COO role for Paul Morgan; Otis CEO Judy Marks to retire
items.summary: Fortune's weekly Power Moves: JLL named Paul Morgan to a newly created chief operating officer post, Otis CEO Judy Marks will retire in the first half of 2027 after a successor is named, Target hired Hilton's Mark Weinstein as Chief Marketing and Guest Experience Officer, and Masco appointed a Chief Technology and AI Officer. The JLL move and the spread of 'AI officer' titles are the most relevant signals for CRE leadership teams.

items.headline: Strategy is dead, long live adaptation: 2026's leaders learn fastest when plans break
items.summary: Barry O'Reilly's counterintuitive trends for 2026 argue the winners will not be the firms with the most polished strategy but those that learn fastest when it breaks, alongside a shift toward regional 'strategic localization' and culture as the durable differentiator as technology commoditizes. JPMorgan's Business Leaders Outlook shows 71% of leaders remain confident in their own company despite a tougher economy. For operators facing a rate shock, this argues for shorter planning cycles and faster feedback loops.

items.headline: 73% of consumers now prioritize healthy aging, led by boomers at 81%
items.summary: Ourvita's 2026 longevity trends report, citing Innova and McKinsey data, finds 73% of global consumers rate healthy aging as very or extremely important — 81% of boomers but also 61% of Gen Z — with boomers prioritizing mobility, joint health, gut health (73%) and heart and immune support (67%). One in three consumers say they now take more ownership of their health. Useful input for wellness programming and dining positioning in senior communities.

items.headline: Gyms and wellness studios become the new 'third place' as burnout reshapes work
items.summary: Wellhub's State of Work-Life Wellness 2026 finds employees moving away from work-hard, play-hard toward building lives around wellbeing, with gyms, studios and outdoor spaces emerging as the new third places where people recharge and connect. Employers are expected to support five pillars — fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition and sleep — and the corporate wellness market is on track to hit $100B in 2026. Relevant to retention strategy for frontline senior living staff, where burnout drives turnover.
